title: You Thought God Forgot You… But Heaven Was Just Getting Started
paragraphs:
You Thought God Forgot You… But Heaven Was Just Getting Started
Why Delay Is Actually a Sign God Is Working
It didn’t feel like God was working.
It felt like silence. Like unanswered prayers stacking up in heaven while your life stayed exactly the same… or worse, started falling apart.
You prayed harder. You cried longer. You tried to stay faithful. But the longer it dragged on, the more it felt like something inside you was quietly breaking.
And somewhere in that silence, a dangerous thought slipped in…
“What if God isn’t listening?”

But what if the delay wasn’t neglect…
What if it was evidence?
Because Scripture doesn’t hide this truth. It confronts it.
When Mary and Martha sent word to Jesus that Lazarus was dying, they expected urgency. They expected movement. They expected immediate intervention.
But the Bible says something that almost feels offensive:
“Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. So, when He heard that Lazarus was ill, He stayed two days longer in the place where He was.” (John 11:5–6)
Read that again.
He loved them… so He stayed.
In the Greek, the word used for “loved” is ἀγαπάω (agapaō) — a deep, covenantal, self-giving love. Not surface-level emotion. Not indifference. Not distraction.
And yet… He delayed.

Because sometimes love doesn’t rush to fix.
Sometimes love allows a deeper miracle to unfold.
By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus was already dead. Four days gone. No hope left. The smell of death had already set in.
Martha met Him with words many of us have whispered in our own way:
“Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” (John 11:21)
That sentence carries disappointment, confusion, and quiet accusation.
Where were You?
But Jesus didn’t apologize for the delay.
He reframed it.
“Did I not tell you that if you believed you would see the glory of God?” (John 11:40)
And then He called into the grave:
“Lazarus, come out.”
And death obeyed.
Because what felt like delay… was actually positioning.
If Jesus had come earlier, Lazarus would have been healed.
But because He delayed, Lazarus was resurrected.
Healing would have been a blessing.
Resurrection became a revelation.
Some of you are begging God for healing in an area where He’s planning resurrection.
And resurrection requires something to look completely dead first.
That’s the part no one wants to talk about.
The Hebrew Scriptures echo this pattern.
In Habakkuk 2:3, it says:
“For still the vision awaits its appointed time… If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come; it will not delay.”
The word “appointed time” comes from the Hebrew מוֹעֵד (mo’ed) — a fixed, divinely scheduled moment. Not random. Not forgotten. Not delayed by accident.
Divinely timed.
Which means your waiting is not empty.
It is calibrated.
Even the word “wait” in Hebrew often carries the sense of tension, like a rope being pulled tight.
You are not being ignored.
You are being stretched.
And stretching always feels like breaking before it feels like strengthening.
The problem is… we measure God’s faithfulness by speed.
But God measures transformation by depth.
And depth takes time.
Think about Joseph.
Betrayed. Sold. Forgotten. Imprisoned.
Years passed with no visible movement from God.
But behind the scenes, God was aligning nations, positioning power, orchestrating famine, and preparing a throne.
Joseph wasn’t delayed.
He was being developed.
What looked like abandonment was actually preparation for influence he couldn’t yet carry.
And maybe that’s what’s happening in your life.
Because if God gave you what you’re asking for right now… would it elevate you, or expose you?
Would it bless you, or break you?
God is not just answering prayers.
He is preparing people.
That’s why Ecclesiastes 3:11 says:
“He has made everything beautiful in its time.”
Not your time.
His.
And the Greek understanding of “time” in the New Testament often separates χρόνος (chronos) — chronological time — from καιρός (kairos) — the appointed, divine moment.
You’re watching the clock.
God is watching the moment.
And when heaven says “now,” nothing can stop what God releases.

Not delay.
Not opposition.
Not even death.
But here’s the tension…
While God is working, you’re still feeling.
You still have nights where your faith feels fragile.
You still wonder if you did something wrong.
You still question if you’ve been forgotten.
Be honest… this hit deeper than you expected.
Not because it’s easy… but because you’re choosing faith anyway.
And listen carefully…
Delay is where many people walk away from God.
But it’s also where the deepest believers are formed.
Because in delay, motives are exposed.
Are you following God for what He gives… or for who He is?
That question changes everything.
Because when the miracle finally comes — and it will — you won’t just celebrate the outcome.
You’ll understand the process.
And you’ll realize something that changes your entire walk with Christ:
God wasn’t late.
He was intentional.
And that realization will anchor your faith in a way instant answers never could.
If this message stirred something in you, don’t keep it to yourself.
You know exactly who came to mind.
If you truly want to glorify God, don’t just consume truth.
Help it reach others.
Support the mission. Share the message. Stay planted in truth.
Because someone else’s breakthrough might be waiting on your obedience to share.
And never forget this—
The silence you fear might be the very place where God is building something you couldn’t survive without.
